collection: NECO BECE Basic Science and Technology supervised JSS 3 practice
note: Original spreadsheet and orthographic drawing classroom tasks with practice marking guides. NECO verifies the paper formats. Historical topic mapping is provisional.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Enter, correct and save a worksheet with accurately labelled data.
questions.prompt: In a supervised spreadsheet session, open a blank workbook. Enter Item and Quantity in A1 and B1. Enter Glue, Tape and Card in A2:A4 with quantities 6, 9 and 12 in B2:B4. A recount finds 7 rolls of Tape. Correct only the affected cell, rename the sheet Supplies, save the workbook as Stock in the assigned folder, and reopen it for inspection.
questions.answer: The Supplies sheet contains Glue 6, Tape 7 and Card 12 under the given headings. The correction is in B3. Reopening Stock displays the saved sheet.
questions.explanation: Editing B3 preserves the other inventory values. Reopening checks that the corrected data persisted.

markingGuide.description: Place the headings and item names in the specified cells.
Enter all final quantities accurately in the corresponding rows.
Name the worksheet Supplies.
Save and reopen Stock from the assigned folder with the corrected data present.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Format numeric cells without changing their underlying values.
questions.prompt: On a classroom computer, create a worksheet with headings Sample and Mass (kg). Enter samples P, Q and R with masses 1.2, 0.75 and 2.375 kg. Use numeric formatting so that the cells display three decimal places, make both headings bold, and widen the mass column so its heading is fully visible. Show the worksheet and the stored values to the teacher.
questions.answer: The displayed masses are 1.200, 0.750 and 2.375. The entries remain numeric with original values 1.2, 0.75 and 2.375. Both headings are bold and the mass heading is fully visible.
questions.explanation: Numeric formatting controls display precision while keeping the entries available for calculation.

markingGuide.description: Enter all three masses as numbers with the correct underlying values.
Display all masses to three decimal places using cell formatting.
Bold both headings.
Set the mass column width so the heading is fully visible.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Use cell references to calculate a total that updates when source data change.
questions.prompt: In a supervised spreadsheet session, put the first two reading-club session counts, 14 and 18, in B2 and B3. In B4 calculate the total with a formula linked to both counts. Show the initial total to the teacher. Change the second count to 21 and show that the total updates without editing B4.
questions.answer: Use =SUM(B2:B3) or =B2+B3 in B4. The result changes from 32 to 35 when B3 becomes 21.
questions.explanation: The formula reads both input cells, so a correction to one input recalculates the result.

markingGuide.description: Enter the original counts in the specified cells.
Put a formula that references both counts in B4.
Show the initial total of 32.
Change B3 to 21 and demonstrate the automatic result of 35.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.learningObjective: Construct and arrange the front, plan and right-side views of a rectangular solid in first-angle projection.
questions.prompt: Use a ruler and set square to draw the front, top and right-side views of a solid rectangular block, 60 mm wide from the front, 30 mm deep and 20 mm high. Work at full size using first-angle projection. Label all three views and dimension the overall width, depth and height once each.
questions.answer: Draw a 60 by 20 mm front view, a 60 by 30 mm plan aligned below it and a 30 by 20 mm right-side view aligned to its left. Label the views and show the three overall dimensions.
questions.explanation: First-angle projection places the top view below the front view and the right-side view to the left. Corresponding widths and heights align.

markingGuide.description: Draw the front rectangle at 60 by 20 mm.
Draw the plan at 60 by 30 mm, aligned below the front.
Draw the right-side view at 30 by 20 mm, aligned to the left of the front.
Label all views and dimension each of the three overall sizes once.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Technology
questions.subtopic: Third-angle views of a stepped block
questions.learningObjective: Project a visible change in height consistently between the front and plan views.
questions.prompt: Draw the front and top views of a stepped block at full size using third-angle projection. Its base is 70 mm wide from the front, 25 mm deep and 15 mm high. A second solid block, 30 mm wide, 25 mm deep and 10 mm high, sits on top, flush with the left, front and back faces of the base. Show visible outlines and edges only. Label both views.
questions.answer: The front outline is 25 mm high across the leftmost 30 mm and 15 mm high across the remaining 40 mm. The top view is a 70 by 25 mm rectangle above the front, with a visible line across its depth 30 mm from the left edge.
questions.explanation: The step changes height in the front view and appears from above as an edge between the two horizontal surfaces.

markingGuide.description: Draw the full 70 mm front width and the 15 mm lower level.
Draw the 30 mm left upper level at an overall height of 25 mm.
Draw the 70 by 25 mm plan above and horizontally aligned with the front.
Show the step edge in the plan 30 mm from the left and label both views.
